source_text: Cernisne quam infesta sit opinioni vestrae gratificatio Dei laudatoris? Dicit eum condere animas, et amare; quod a vobis negatur, qui iuratis innocentium animas esse sub diabolo, et exosas Deo; cum nihil habeant aliud, quam quod ab auctore sortitae sunt.
pass_a_gloss: Do you perceive how hostile the gratification of the praiser of God is to your opinion? He says he founds souls and loves them; which is denied by you, who swear that the souls of innocents are under the devil and hated by God; when they have nothing else than what they have received from the author.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: Do you see how hostile this grateful praise of God is to your opinion? It says that he creates souls and loves them. You deny this, swearing that innocent souls are under the devil and hated by God, though they possess nothing except what they received from their author.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
